faq.q: Why is the start line drawn in pencil?
faq.a: Pencil is graphite, which does not dissolve in the solvent. Ink would dissolve and run up the paper, mixing with your results.
asks: Why not use a pen for the line?

faq.q: Why do some dyes travel further?
faq.a: Dyes that dissolve better in the solvent and stick less to the paper are carried further up. Each dye has its own balance, so they spread apart.
A chromatogram is the finished strip of paper showing the separated spots. You look at how many spots there are and how far each one moved.

faq.q: How can chromatography show a substance is pure?
faq.a: A pure substance gives only one spot. A mixture of dyes gives two or more spots.
asks: How many spots does a pure substance make?

faq.a: Rf is the distance a spot moved divided by the distance the solvent moved, so it is always between 0 and 1. The same dye in the same solvent always gives the same Rf.

facts: Rf value = distance moved by the spot divided by distance moved by the solvent front.
A pure substance produces a single spot on a chromatogram.

quiz.say: A spot moved 3 cm and the solvent moved 6 cm. What is the Rf value?
quiz.show: A spot moved 3 cm and the solvent moved 6 cm. What is the Rf value?
quiz.why: Rf is 3 divided by 6, which is 0.5.

wrong.1: That divides the wrong way round; Rf is never more than 1.
wrong.2: 3 cm is only the spot distance; you must divide by the solvent distance.

quiz.say: A food colouring gives three spots. What does that tell you?
quiz.show: A food colouring gives three spots. What does that tell you?

options.show: It is a mixture of at least three dyes
options.say: It is a mixture of at least three dyes

quiz.why: Each spot is a different dye, so the colouring is a mixture.

wrong.0: A pure substance gives only one spot.
wrong.1: The spots are the dyes themselves.
